paper.title_en: A physical connection criterion for reaction-coordinate reduction in quantum-field tunneling
paper.abstract_en:
Reaction-coordinate descriptions of quantum-field tunneling are predictive only when the
eliminated field-space directions are controlled at the accuracy of the target decay observable.
We formulate this requirement as a physical connection criterion. At finite ultraviolet cutoff
and finite volume, the regulated stationary Schr\"odinger equation is decomposed along a
tunneling characteristic and reduced by an exact Feshbach--Schur projection. The exact
projected dynamics defines a physically normalized connection coefficient, while a candidate
local second-order reaction-coordinate equation defines a comparator coefficient. The reduction
is accepted when their absolute or logarithmic discrepancy is below the prescribed target error.
The dominant-channel locality hypothesis (DCLH) supplies the local Sturm--Liouville comparator
and a residual bound on the physical solution class, and we prove that this residual controls
the physical connection map and simple connection/Jost zeros. The criterion extends to
regulator families through renormalized connection data, cutoff-uniform reduction control,
and the subsequent infinite-volume spectral limit. Thus the primary result is a certification
framework and finite-regulator stability theorem; interacting-QFT realizations remain
model-specific benchmarks. Once the local reduction is certified, any suitable connection
solver may be used. We develop exact WKB as one realization: Airy--Stokes matching defines
the higher connection correction, and known one- and two-loop false-vacuum results provide
normalization and reconstruction benchmarks.
